grand_strategy.reading:
Latvia is the textbook case of Luttwak's weak-state strategy: a country of 1.9
million with a long border and a large Russian-speaking population cannot win
an attritional contest with Russia, so it plays the paradoxical game of making
itself too costly to attack and too connected to be left alone. Every pillar
borrows weight from outside: the Canadian-led brigade and Article 5 for
deterrence, EU money and the escape clause for the budget, German and American
factories for the kit, Lithuania's terminal for the gas. The strategy is
consistent but its cost is dependence on partners whose own commitment is
wavering (US rotation gaps, weapons delays, the Pentagon posture review) and on
an internal politics that has shown it can fall to a single drone: the May 2026
crisis, the 52% turnout and 25% of the vote for two populist parties, one
openly pro-Russian, are the soft flank. Russia is graded adversary because the
Latvian state itself names it the existential threat and a sponsor of terrorism,
not because Riga seeks its regime's end; Belarus is a rival whose pressure is
cheap to apply and costly to stop. Two signals that are not rows: the
Silina government fell over an air-defence failure, not over foreign policy
(Kulbergs, who took over, promised to hold defence at 5% of GDP and keep a hard
line on Moscow), and part of the Russian-speaking population is still outside
the citizenry (non-citizens were 9% of residents in 2024), so the election
measures only part of the minority's weight.

stances.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded from adversary to rival for consistency with Estonia and Lithuania; 'adversary' is reserved for actors seeking each other's destruction (Iran-Israel). The Saeima's 'state sponsor of terrorism' declaration and the chargé-level relations are the hardest posture in NATO, but Riga's aim is deterrence and a Russian defeat in Ukraine, not the end of the Russian state. The Latvian state itself uses the vocabulary of the mortal enemy: the State Security Service (VDD) puts Russia's services at the head of the threats to the state and a secondary account of its February 2026 report calls Russia an existential threat; the Saeima declared Russia a state sponsor of terrorism on 11 Aug 2022 (67 votes, none against); relations were cut to charge d'affaires level on 24 Feb 2023; and Latvian soil has seen Russian-directed arson cells (cases of 2023-25), GPS jamming from Kaliningrad, and Russian rail crossings shut from 1 Jul 2026. Adversary rather than rival because the declared Latvian aim is Russia's defeat in Ukraine and the Russian state is named the threat to Latvia's existence, not a competitor. The case against: Riga seeks no change of regime in Moscow, keeps an embassy, and still sold EUR 962.5m of goods to Russia in 2025 (4.9% of exports), so the grade is the harder of two readings (the 'rival' reading is the fallback). Bond - grievance: the 1940 occupation and the Soviet deportations, and more than a third of residents who are not ethnic Latvians, mostly Russian-speaking.

stances_toward.note: Canada's own side, rewritten from the provisional reciprocal: Canada is the framework nation of the NATO Multinational Brigade at Adazi (a battlegroup since 2017, a brigade from 2024), paid EUR 18.5m for the barracks and confirmed in July 2026 that more than 2,000 troops stay until 2031, its largest standing deployment in Europe. Ally by the NATO treaty and by the commitment itself; warming because it grew from battlegroup to brigade and now has an end date pushed out five years. Bond affinity: the Latvian diaspora in Canada and Canada's non-recognition of the Soviet annexation (Latvia's card). For Ottawa this is where its NATO credibility is exposed in the field, and the most visible proof, to Washington and to Europe, of the 5% pledge.

stances_toward.note: Neutral from Beijing's side, and lower than Riga's own reading. Latvia quit the 16+1 with Estonia on 11 Aug 2022, and no Chinese Foreign Ministry comment on the two withdrawals was found: an RFE/RL snapshot says Beijing had not yet addressed them publicly, so the exit carried no visible cost. The sources read show no Taiwan office and no 5G order against Latvia. The one friction is Latvia's own: the VDD 2026 report names Chinese services among the national-security threats, and Beijing's answer to that is not in the sources read. Neutral means no significant posture from Beijing, not warmth. Confidence C: the grade rests on a silence and on a missing response; a Chinese statement would make it firmer. Bond none.

relations_from.summary: Latvia is one of 14 states that signed a January 2026 statement treating false-flag or undocumented shadow-fleet tankers as stateless vessels that can be detained, and asked the EU in February 2026 for a full ban on maritime services for Russian vessels; unlike Sweden or Germany it has made no reported seizure, and bunkering outside port is not prohibited.

relations_from.summary: The Swedish authorities seized the Vezhen in January 2025 over damage to the Sweden-Latvia subsea cable in the Baltic; attribution to Russia is unproven and the Swedish security police chief warns against jumping to it.

relations_from.summary: Latvia has kept the Silene crossing closed since 19 Sep 2023 and stopped nearly 10,000 illegal crossing attempts in the first eight months of 2026 (12,046 in 2025), including two tunnels found in August 2026; the Prosecutor General opened a criminal case in mid-July 2026 against Belarusian border officials, and the government declined on 5 Aug 2026 to close the last crossing, Paternieki.

relations_from.summary: On 13 Feb 2018 FinCEN named ABLV, Latvia's second-largest bank, an institution of primary money laundering concern (shell-company activity, links to North Korea's missile procurement); the bank was wound down, Latvia banned banking for shell companies and non-resident deposits fell about 38% in the first half of 2018 as the model was dismantled.
relations_from.note: The current non-resident deposit share was not found; the 2018 figures are historical context. Five banks held 87.2% of assets at end-2025.
